newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar on Wednesday in dull trading, dealers said.
"The market continues to be extremely quiet. Trading was affected by the sterling's slide abroad, which pushed the basket downwards," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The Bank of Israel was forced to intervene in the market after the basket fell to more than seven percent below the diagonal rate. The central bank bought almost $100 million," she said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3730 shekels against 3.3680 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6504 shekels against 3.6502 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7477 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7681 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9757 shekels after 1.9745 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3710 shekels.
